links.reason: The invocation praises one who kept nothing for himself (தனக்கென்று ஒன்றானும் உள்ளான்) and toiled for others; it says nothing of giving away self or wives, which is what Neelakesi 243 attacks (தன்னை யீந்ததும் தாரங்க ளீந்தது). The tension is with a gift the Kundalakesi verse never names, so the claim that the quarrel is visible in this pair needs the birth-story background supplied from outside.

Neelakesi 427 says it is the unforgetting yoga activity (யோக பாவம்) that brings the stain back, which supplies a mechanism for the Kural's மற்றீண்டு வாரா நெறி; that extends rather than limits the couplet, so develops fits better. The objection that a freed self could be bound again is the opponent's, not in either printed verse, so the Kural-side gain is thin.

760 says sound has form (உருவாதலின்) and so cannot rest in formless space; 516 argues only that sound is heard later because it must travel to the organ (பொறியுறுகாறும் வரலின்). That sound is matter is inferred in 516, not stated, so the 'same premise' needs a generous reading, though the two uses against two opponents are real.

736 has the Sankhya call the soul எங்கும் உளன், present everywhere, and 765 turns that pervasion against him: if they were joined everywhere before (எங்கும் இவை முன்னும் புல்லினவே), a new union (புணர்ச்சி புதிது) means nothing. A claim and the reply that undoes it, and the note says which.
links.text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain: இல்லுளி (765.1) is obscure and 736.2 is hard to divide.

links.reason: The Manimekalai's image is of both parents (தாய் கண்ணகியையும் ... தாதை கோவலன் தன்னையும் கடவுள் எழுதிய படிமம்) and a pathini goddess speaks (பத்தினிக் கடவுள் ஆங்கு உரைப்போள்), so the note's facts hold; but nothing says this is Senguttuvan's shrine or that the epic 'reshapes the cult toward the household', which is the teaches sentence's whole point.

Neelakesi 610 grants a continuity only along an unbroken branch from root to flower (அடியொடு பூவின் இடையறவின்றி நெடியதோர் கொம்பு) and charges a gap (இடை பாழ்) between man and god; the Manimekalai's தொடர்ச்சி example is seed, sprout and stalk called paddy (வித்து முளை தாள் ... நெல் என வழங்குதல்). The note calls 610's image seed-to-flower, which the Tamil does not say, and the Manimekalai example is about naming, not rebirth, so the pairing is a related doctrine rather than one argument answered.

The lute does pass into Madhavi's hand in the screened bower (வசந்த மாலைகைத் திருந்துகோல் நல்லியாழ் செவ்வனம் வாங்கி) and in 7 the parting is put on the music and on karma (யாழ்இசைமேல் வைத்துத்தன் ஊழ்வினைவந்து உருத்தது). But a place of pleasure becoming a place of parting is a reversal in story order, not two incompatible claims, so tension is the wrong type.

392 is Mokkalan's demand for the bearer of arising, persisting and perishing, and 403 is a Jain reply using the calf and the bull (ஏறாய காலத்து ... எழாத குழக்கன்றினுக்கு இன்மை முன்னா). The horn on which the note and teaches rest is not named in 403's Tamil, and the verse is too unclear to say it answers 392 specifically.
links.text_issue: 403 flagged uncertain; கலைக்கு (line 4) unclear and the horn is supplied by the marker.

links.reason: Neelakesi 218 offers the wife who burns with her husband (கணவனோடு ஈமத்தின் வேம் அவட்கும் விழுக்குணம் ஆம் கொலோ) as an absurd consequence; in the Manimekalai the fire spares Aathirai because her husband is alive (பக்கம் சேர்ந்தனன் ... வந்தனன் தோன்றும்), and she is likened to Lakshmi on the lotus. The fire is not a judgment on the pyre death as virtue, so 'neither epic lets it stand as achieved virtue' misreads the Buddhist scene.

The Manimekalai's Jain gives the gram whose nature is not lost when it becomes a dish while the gram perishes (பயற்றுத் தன்மை கெடாது கும்மாயம் இயற்றி அப் பயறு அழிதலும்), and Neelakesi 312 the gold that persists as pot becomes crown (செம்பொன்னால் நிலையுதலும் சிதைவு ஆக்கம்), applied to souls as men and gods (நரர்தேவர் உயிர்களையும்). The pair tests a polemical report against the school's own example and it holds.

49 has the sage know he will make her see her powerlessness (தெருட்டுவேன் இவள் திறமின்மை) and 56 has her confess that this victor has no magic but virtue (விச்சை வேறிலன் விழுக்குணமுடையன்) and that she cannot come before him unless he wills it. A foreknowledge and its fulfilment, as the note says.

Neelakesi 878 asks what cause joins the elements (பூதங்கள் சேர்வதற்கு ஏது என்); Tirumanthiram 1805 calls maya, the instruments, elements and senses the fivefold work of grace (அருள்ஐந்து மாம் அருட் செய்கையே). Neither verse says the Jain leaves the cause 'in the soul and its deeds', and 1805 is not addressed to materialists, so the qualification and both gains are built on what the texts leave unsaid.

Neelakesi 255 sneers at chewing a creature's red flesh once it has died (செத்த பொழுதின் அச் செந்தடி மென்றிடும்); Kural 258 says the faultless do not eat flesh parted from life (உயிரின் தலைப்பிரிந்த ஊன்), which covers all flesh. Both refuse such meat, so the pair agrees; the Kural adds no condition to the epic's view.

Mokkalan's reductio says that if wasting the body (காயம் வாட்டி) were good, burning or wasting with disease would be penance; Kural 261 makes உற்றநோய் நோன்றல் half of tapas. The note states that the conflict depends on whether உற்ற means self-imposed or what comes unsought, and the views are correctly put in Mokkalan's mouth.

Puram 264's rite (பதுக்கை, செம்பூங் கண்ணி, மயிற் பீலி, பெயர் பொறித்து ... நட்டனரே கல்லும்) is a hero-stone; the epic unit has a jewelled image, flowers (பூப்பலி), sacrifice and festival, with no stone, name or feather named in these lines. The link runs through the kaathai's title and is real, but the unit does not show the adaptation the teaches describes, and 'herdsmen' is not in Puram 264.

Neelakesi 627 argues that since perishing is total, the release he speaks of must be that perishing (கேடது தான் முழுதாதலின் நீசொல்லும் வீடது வாகலும் வேண்டும்); the Manimekalai teacher puts release in seeing that the links are unstable and without self (நிலையா ... ஆன்மா இலை என இப்படி உணரும் இவை வீட்டு இயல்பு ஆம்). Incompatible accounts of Buddhist release, correctly attributed.

120 names நயன் among the doors (வைப்பு நயன் அளவை), and 819 reasons from the side of the bearer and of the quality (குணிக்கண் நோக்கின் ... குணத்தணிக்கண் நோக்கின்), which is standpoint reasoning. But 820 and the opponent's being won are not in the packet, and both verses are uncertain, so 'the very tool that ends the debate' overstates.
links.text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain; நான்மை and துருநெறி (819) unclear.

links.reason: Both verses use the medical frame: 116 பிணி ... தீர்தற்குரிய திரியோக மருந்து, 724 சாதி முதலாப் பிணி ... திரிதோடம் ... தீர்ப்பது மெய்யுணர்வு. That is a real recurrence, but nothing in 724 shows the defeated opponent offered treatment rather than condemnation, which is what the teaches sentence claims.

The Neelakesi sage says she has bathed, scented and garlanded herself but has covered with skin a body leaking filth (ஒழுக்கு ஊற்றைப் பல்பண்டம் மூடினாய் தோலின்); Manimekalai says flowers, paste, cloth and jewels hide the flesh's smell (பூவினும் சாந்தினும் புலால் மறைத்து யாத்து தூசினும் அணியினும்). The shared image is specific, and the reversal of the sexes of ascetic and tempted is a true and useful point.

The Charana's rule (ஒழிகென ஒழியாது ஊட்டும் வல்வினை ... ஒழிக்கவும் ஒண்ணா) does match the quatrain's உறற்பால நீக்கல் உறுவர்க்கும் ஆகா. But the epic gain speaks of 'the Charana's silence about the couple's fate' when in this unit he states the rule aloud, and his not grieving and inner lamp are not in these lines; the unit also adds release through the Jina's word (ஓதிய வேதத்து ஒளிஉறின்), which the note ignores.

In the bridal chamber the swan, beaten by Kannaki's gait, hides in the pools (அன்னம் நல்நுதல் மெல்நடைக்கு அழிந்து நல்நீர்ப் பண்ணை ... செறியவும்); on the shore Kovalan tells the swan not to follow a shore girl, since it cannot match her walk (சேரல் மடஅன்னம் சேரல் நடைஒவ்வாய்). The same compliment moving to another woman before Madhavi is a true and pointed reading of the pair.

Neelakesi 86 confines release by penance to those of the land of deeds (கரும நிலத்தார் கருவினை போய்த் தான் உயர் இன்பம் தவத்தால் தலைப்படும்), while Naladiyar 37 is about how to use human birth's gains (உடம்பிற்கே ஒப்புரவு செய்தொழுகாது). The limit is real, but the quatrain is about misusing the gain, not who has it, and its உம்பர் is heaven, not release.
links.text_issue: 86 flagged uncertain; ஆவிதையம் may be corrupt.

links.reason: The shared premise holds: Maadalan's list ends மீக்கூற்றாளர் யாவரும் இன்மையின் யாக்கை நில்லாது, and Puram 363 says the kings went to the burning ground (சுடுபிணக் காடுபதி யாகப் போகி) and ends முந்நீர் வரைப்பகம் முழுதுடன் துறந்தே. But Maadalan's counsel of sacrifice, on which the tension rests, is not in this unit.
links.text_issue: The counsel of a great sacrifice lies after line 154, outside the linked unit.

links.reason: Kural 650 blames those who do not expound what they have learned (கற்றது உணர விரித்துரையாதார்); 'unable' is Pope's word, not the couplet's, so the step from inability to deliberate silence is weaker than stated. And 683 does itself state the norm (any common man who tells the good he sees is greater, சாத்தனும் யானும் ... நன்மை கண்டாலும் நினக்குரைத்து), so the epic-side gain is false.

Neelakesi 18 sets householders who keep giving and conduct (தானமொடு சீலம்) beside those who leave home to wear down their deeds (செய்வினைகள் நைய முயல்வாரும்), without ranking them or replying to anyone. Reading it as an answer to Kural 46's புறத்தாற்றில் போஒய்ப் பெறுவது எவன், naming a gain the household cannot give, puts a claim in the verse it does not make.
links.text_issue: 18 flagged uncertain; line 3's division is doubtful.

links.reason: Tirumular puts those who said 'kill, stab' (கொல்லிடு குத்தென்று கூறிய மாக்களை) in fire-mouthed hell (தீவாய் நரகிடை); Neelakesi 97 names the sin of eating flesh beside that of killing (கொன்ற பாவம் ... தின்ற பாவம்) and has both burn in the fire's mouth. Each carries guilt past the striker, in opposite directions, and the pairing shows it.

Tirumular asks that merit and sin both be uprooted (இரண்டையும் வேர்அறத் தப்புற). In the Silappathikaram the monkey's small hand on the god's body is shown as proof that he gained this form through the gift (சாயலன் மனைவி தானந் தன்னால் ஆயினன் இவ்வடிவு அறிமினோ); the epic praises the gift's fruit. Reading the hand as a sign that merit binds is imposed on the tale.

Manimekalai's 'if for the body, who cast your son into the burning ground?' (உடற்கு அழுதனையேல் ... எடுத்துப் புறங்காட்டு இட்டனர் யாரே) presupposes Tirumular's town that wails, calls him a corpse, burns him and forgets (சூரையங் காட்டிடைக் கொண்டுபோய்ச் சுட்டிட்டு). The second horn, pity for every life (எவ் உயிர்க்கு ஆயினும் இரங்கல் வேண்டும்), is the epic's real addition.

The preface's Nannan is of Peruvaayil (பெருவாயில் நன்னனை), his tree a vakai (பொன்படு வாகை), killed by Narmudi Cheral; Kuruntokai 73's Nannan loses a mango (நறுமா) to the Kosar. Nothing fixes them as one chief, so the 'disagreement' joins two men by name alone, and the teaches sentence is speculation either way.

The venba says the moonlit night was like the king's umbrella, cool to the joined and hot to others (கூடினார் பால் நிழலாய்க் கூடார்ப்பால் வெய்தாய்), for Madhavi and Kannaki; Kural 1229's woman says the town reels when evening spreads (பதிமருண்டு பைதல் உழக்கும்). Neither text treats the other's claim, and the 'projection of grief' is the linker's reading, not something either verse shows; a shared evening theme dressed up as a qualification.

Neelakesi 138 says the sage made her who came to kill him bow by his virtues (கொல்லக் கருதி வந்தேனைக் குணங்களாலே வணங்குவித்த); Kural 314 says to punish by doing good to the wrongdoer (நன்னயஞ் செய்து). The sage does no good deed to her here; he conquers by his qualities, so the couplet's punishment-by-kindness fits only loosely, and the verse two later is not in the packet.

The goddess's afterthought மக்கள் யாக்கை உணவின் பிண்டம் shares Kudapulaviyanar's உண்டி முதற்றே உணவின் பிண்டம, and the note calls it the same phrase, not a quotation. The king's duty to feed by tanks against a mantra that ends one renouncer's hunger (இப் பெரு மந்திரம் இரும் பசி அறுக்கும்) is a real and specific contrast.
links.text_issue: manimekalai:10:71-93 flagged uncertain at 83-85, which the link does not use.

links.reason: The goddess says that when a former deed rises, penance does not help those not upright (உம்மை வினைவந் துருத்த காலைச் செம்மையிலோர்க்குச் செய்தவம் உதவாது); Naladiyar 51 lets sin stand once merit is spent (நல்வினை தீர்விடத்து நிற்குமாம் தீது). Two different limits on austerity, the one of time and the other moral, are correctly set side by side.
links.text_issue: Unit flagged uncertain; who the செம்மையிலோர் are is not stated.

links.reason: Thirikadugam counts living as kin of the unlearned (கல்லார்க்கு இனனாய் ஒழுகலும்) among ruins born of ignorance; Kural 451 says smallness takes small company as kin (சிறுமைதான் சுற்றமாச் சூழ்ந்து விடும்). Both condemn low company; the 'cause and result' the teaches names are the verse's own frame, not something the pairing teaches.

628 says one who does not chase pleasure meets no pain (இன்பம் விழையான் ... துன்பம் உறுதல் இலன்); 669 says do the deed that yields joy despite pain (துன்பம் உறவரினும் செய்க ... இன்பம் பயக்கும் வினை). They advise on different matters, attitude and the choice of tasks, and the teaches sentence concedes as much; a shared pair of words is not a tension.

Naladiyar 47's fool hails a pot oozing from nine openings because dark skin covers it (ஈப் போர்த்த கருந்தோலால் கண்விளக்கப்பட்டு); Neelakesi 108 has men perish for a filthy body, a cover full of worms (புழுக்குலங்களால் நிறைத்த போர்வை ... அழுக்குடம்பு), set beside an evil rebirth (தீக்கதி) and a stained lineage (விழுக்குலங்கள் மாசுபடும்). The sermon's three reckonings against the quatrain's one is a true development.

The kuravai stanza takes up Natrinai 34's words: மார்பு தருவெந்நோய் for மார்பு தர வந்த படர் மலி அரு நோய், the kadamba garland, and மடவன் for மடவை மன்ற. The step to 'more foolish than the velan' (வேலன் தன்னினுந் தான்மடவன்) and the setting inside a hymn of praise are real additions, and both gains hold.

Neelakesi 685 says that if silence proved knowledge, infants, this tree and the mountain would share that greatness (பிள்ளைகளும் மற்றிம் மரமு மலையும் அம்மாண்பின); Tirumular calls silence of speech alone muteness (வாக்கு மவுனத்து வந்தாலும் மூங்கையாம்). Both deny outward silence as proof and move the test in opposite directions, as stated.
links.text_issue: 685 line 2 hard to divide; flagged uncertain.

links.reason: In 18 Manimekalai tells the prince the human body is a vessel of suffering (இடும்பைக் கொள்கலம் மக்கள் யாக்கை) and expects warriors not to heed women's wisdom (பெண்டிர் கூறும் பேர் அறிவு உண்டோ); in 20 she makes him look, feature by feature, and charges him with not seeing (வஞ்சம் தெரியாய்). The later scene answers the failure the earlier one foresees.
links.text_issue: The b span 18:124-141 is not a marked unit; the marked unit runs to 142.

links.reason: Champapathi does liken the offer to the false word that killing is dharma (கொலை அறம் ஆம் எனும் ... படிற்று உரை), but her refusal rests first on her inability: a departed life goes by its deeds and to bring it back is not in her power (ஈங்கு எனக்கு ஆவது ஒன்று அன்று). Kural 259 weighs sacrifice against not killing and eating; the self-offering 'extension' and the epic-side gain both overstate the passing comparison.

Kural 356 has those who learn here and see the true thing (கற்றீண்டு மெய்ப்பொருள் கண்டார்) reach the path of no return; Neelakesi 658 says those of any form who understand the Lord's scripture reach release by order (எவ்வுருவினாரும் முறையினால் எய்துவர்). Naming the scripture, opening it to any form against the couplet's ஈண்டு, and making it gradual are real qualifications.
links.text_issue: 658 has several repaired TSCII characters and is flagged uncertain.

links.reason: The Silappathikaram's image weeps without speaking when the sceptre bends (நாவொடு நவிலாது நவைநீர் உகுத்துப் பாவைநின்று அழுஉம்); the Manimekalai's is a speaking image (நா உடைப் பாவை) that tells the city she brings rain (மழை தரும் இவள்). The verbal contrast is exact and the pair shows a sign set against an active witness.

Both have the tiger refuse prey fallen on its left: Puram 190 கேழல் இடம்பட வீழ்ந்தென அன்று அவண் உண்ணாது, Naladiyar 300 இடம்வீழ்ந்தது உண்ணாது இறக்கும். The Puram makes it a pattern for choosing friends and the Naladiyar for refusing even heaven at the cost of honour (மானம் மழுங்க வரின்), which is a true and specific difference of use.
